RDES support

Source: RDES.md

RDML7 supports the Real-time PCR Data Essential Spreadsheet Format (RDES) v1.0.

RDES is a UTF-8, tab-separated, LF-newline text format for exactly one qPCR run. Amplification and melting data are stored in separate files.

Import

Single amplification or melting file:

x <- readRDML(
  "run_amplification.tsv",
  format = "rdes"
)

Import an amplification + melting pair into the same run:

x <- readRDML(
  "run_amplification.tsv",
  format = "rdes",
  companionFile = "run_melting.tsv",
  expId = "experiment1",
  runId = "run1"
)

RDES is automatically detected for .tsv, and by header sniffing for .csv or .txt. The content is still tab-separated even when the extension is .csv or .txt, as specified by RDES.

Export

If the selected run contains only one curve type:

writeRDML(
  x,
  "run.tsv",
  format = "rdes"
)

Explicit amplification or melting export:

writeRDML(
  x,
  "run.tsv",
  format = "rdes",
  expId = "experiment1",
  runId = "run1",
  rdesType = "adp"
)

Write both RDES files:

paths <- writeRDML(
  x,
  "run.tsv",
  format = "rdes",
  expId = "experiment1",
  runId = "run1",
  rdesType = "both"
)

This creates:

run_amplification.tsv
run_melting.tsv

Multiple Tm values

RDES permits multiple Tm values separated by semicolons. The current RDML7 dataType model stores one numeric meltTemp; therefore import keeps the first Tm and warns. The full melting fluorescence curve is retained.
